q: How do I check whether my project depends on a server?
a: Open File ▸ Project Settings ▸ General (`file.projectSettings.general`). The first line says Project file: on a local disk, or Project file: on a network share with the share's type and server, e.g. (cifs, //nas/media) (`projectSettings.storage.project`). If any clips are on shares, the next line counts them: Clips on network shares: 3 of 12 (`projectSettings.storage.clips`). In the Project panel (Media Pool in the Resolve workflow) each such clip also has a grey NET badge.

q: What does the Project file line at the top of Project Settings mean?
a: It tells you where the saved project file lives: Project file: on a local disk, or Project file: on a network share followed by the share's type and server, such as (cifs, //nas/media) (`projectSettings.storage.project`). It's in File ▸ Project Settings ▸ General (`file.projectSettings.general`). A project that has never been saved shows no line.

q: What do I see when I hover the NET badge on a clip?
a: The share the clip's file is on and its type, for example On a network share: //nas/media (cifs). The grey NET badge sits next to the clip's other badges in the Project panel (Media Pool in the Resolve workflow), in both list and icon view.

q: Does the network badge appear in icon view or only in list view?
a: Both. In the Project panel (Media Pool in the Resolve workflow) a clip whose file is on a network share shows a grey NET badge next to its other badges in list view and in icon view; hover it to see the share.

q: I unmounted the share; how long until the badges update?
a: A few seconds. Revolution re-reads the system's mount table every few seconds, so a share you mount or unmount is reflected in the NET badges and in Project Settings ▸ General shortly after; nothing needs refreshing by hand.

q: Is a Plasma network folder from Dolphin treated as a network share?
a: Yes. Shares mounted by Plasma (Dolphin's Network places, through kio-fuse), GNOME's gvfs, /etc/fstab or autofs all count. Revolution recognises SMB / CIFS, NFS, sshfs, rclone, kio-fuse, gvfs and a few others.

q: What does media.storage return when I give it one clip?
a: Run `media.storage` with `{"item": <id>}` to ask about that clip; without it, it answers for the project file and every file clip. The result is `{"project": {"kind": "network", "fsType": "cifs", "source": "//nas/media"}, "items": [{"item", "path", "storage"}], "networkItems": n}`, where kind is local, network or unknown (unknown on systems other than Linux for now).

q: Why is editing straight off a home server riskier than off a local SSD?
a: A mounted share looks like an ordinary folder but isn't one: reads are slower than a local disk, the share can stop answering when the server sleeps or the Wi-Fi drops, and saving over it isn't always as safe as saving locally. That's why Revolution first works out where each file lives (the NET badge, the storage lines in Project Settings ▸ General) and takes extra care only with the files on shares.

q: Does Revolution open my media files to work out whether they are remote?
a: No. It looks only at the system's mount table, never at the file itself, so the answer comes at once, even while the server is down or asleep.

q: Why is there no storage line in Project Settings for my new project?
a: The Project file line appears once the project has been saved: an unsaved project has no file yet, so it shows no line. The Clips on network shares line appears only when at least one clip is on a share. Save the project (File ▸ Save, `file.save`) and look again in File ▸ Project Settings ▸ General (`file.projectSettings.general`).

q: Do Resolve or Premiere show which clips are on network storage?
a: Neither shows this; Revolution's NET badge and the storage lines in Project Settings ▸ General are its own (a fork feature). Resolve and Premiere just show media as offline when a share vanishes.

q: And which network systems does that detection understand?
a: SMB / CIFS, NFS, sshfs, rclone, GNOME / Plasma network folders (kio-fuse, gvfs) and a few others. It reads the mount table only, so even a sleeping server gets an instant answer.
